fields.summary: Comprehensive care for acne scarring — medical consultations, prescriptions where necessary, and RF microneedling and laser treatments to reduce scarring, under the supervision of one of our physicians.

faqs.question: How does care for acne scarring start?
faqs.answer: With a medical consultation — from there, a physician may recommend a prescription where necessary, alongside treatments like RF microneedling and laser.

faqs.question: Is this care physician-supervised?
faqs.answer: Yes — every step, from consultation to treatment, is supervised by one of our physicians.

faqs.question: Which treatment is used for acne scarring?
faqs.answer: RF microneedling and laser treatments are options for acne scarring. Your physician will discuss which options suit your skin during your consultation.

faqs.question: Will a prescription always be part of my care?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — prescriptions are provided where necessary, based on your physician's assessment.

faqs.question: How do I book a consultation?
faqs.answer: Through Mikata, our external booking system. For all aesthetic treatment appointments, book a 20-minute consultation with Dr. Farhat.

fields.summary: Calgary's dry climate can contribute to dry, uncomfortable skin. The clinic's RF microneedling approach includes topical products such as moisturizers and pigment regulators. Your physician will assess whether this approach is appropriate for your skin.

faqs.question: Why is Calgary's climate mentioned for dry skin care?
faqs.answer: Calgary's dry climate can contribute to dry, uncomfortable skin.

faqs.question: How does RF micro-needling help with dry skin?
faqs.answer: The clinic's approach uses RF microneedling with topical products, including moisturizers and pigment regulators. Your physician will discuss suitability and the risks and benefits of the proposed products.

faqs.question: How long does the nourishing effect last?
faqs.answer: The response and its duration vary. Your physician can discuss what to expect for your skin and the proposed treatment.

fields.summary: Fine lines and wrinkles develop as skin gradually loses collagen and elasticity. Blue Diamond Medical offers radiofrequency and RF microneedling treatments that may soften their appearance and firm the skin, planned around your skin type and goals during a consultation.

faqs.question: What treatments address fine lines and wrinkles?
faqs.answer: RF microneedling and radiofrequency skin tightening may soften fine lines and wrinkles. Your physician will assess which treatment suits your skin.

faqs.question: Is treatment the same for everyone?
faqs.answer: No — each treatment is planned around your own skin during a consultation.

faqs.question: Do these treatments also help with skin tightening, not just lines?
faqs.answer: Yes, these treatments may also help with skin tightening. Your physician will assess which options are suitable for your skin.

fields.summary: Razor bumps form when shaved hairs curl back into the skin, and they can be uncomfortable and prone to infection where ingrown hairs are also present. Laser hair removal at Blue Diamond Medical addresses the underlying cause by reducing the hair that produces them, which may improve both comfort and skin texture. Results vary, and a consultation confirms whether the treatment suits your skin and hair type.

faqs.question: Why are razor bumps a concern beyond appearance?
faqs.answer: Razor bumps can be uncomfortable. The affected skin can sometimes become infected.

faqs.question: Does treatment just remove the bumps, or address the cause?
faqs.answer: By reducing hair growth, laser hair removal may help reduce the ingrown hairs that cause razor bumps. Results vary.

faqs.question: Which treatment is used for razor bumps?
faqs.answer: Laser hair removal.

faqs.question: Is this a minimally invasive treatment?
faqs.answer: Laser hair removal is a non-surgical treatment.

fields.summary: Rosacea can cause redness that is distressing to live with. Care starts with a medical consultation to discuss your symptoms and treatment options. Laser treatment may help with visible redness and blood vessels.

faqs.question: Where does treatment for rosacea and redness start?
faqs.answer: With a full medical consultation to discuss what can realistically be achieved for your specific presentation.

faqs.question: What treatment is generally used for rosacea and redness?
faqs.answer: Laser treatment may help with visible redness and blood vessels. Your physician will assess your rosacea and discuss suitable options.

faqs.question: Will rosacea come back after treatment?
faqs.answer: Results and their duration vary by individual — your physician will discuss realistic expectations for your case during the consultation.

faqs.question: Is rosacea the same as general facial redness?
faqs.answer: Rosacea is one cause of facial redness; a physician consultation is the way to understand what's contributing to your specific redness.

fields.summary: Skin loses firmness as the collagen and elastin that support it gradually decline. Radiofrequency treatment at Blue Diamond Medical warms the deeper layers of the skin to encourage collagen production, which may help tighten and smooth areas of laxity on the face and body. Sessions take about 15 minutes, most patients find them comfortable, and downtime is usually minimal. Results vary, and a consultation confirms whether the treatment suits you.

faqs.question: How does radio-frequency treatment address skin laxity?
faqs.answer: It promotes collagen and elastin production, which helps tighten and smooth skin across the body.

faqs.question: How long does a session take?
faqs.answer: About 15 minutes.

faqs.question: Is there downtime after treatment?
faqs.answer: This treatment is not typically associated with downtime, though your physician will confirm what to expect for the area being treated.

fields.summary: Harsh weather and daily stresses can leave skin looking tired. A session takes under 45 minutes and can leave skin looking refreshed, with a natural glow and a softer appearance to fine lines and wrinkles.

faqs.question: How long does a skin revitalization treatment take?
faqs.answer: Under 45 minutes.

faqs.question: What does skin revitalization address?
faqs.answer: Skin that looks tired from harsh weather and daily stress, including the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.

faqs.question: Which treatments are used for skin revitalization?
faqs.answer: Laser Skin Treatments and RF microneedling.

fields.summary: Damaged blood vessels under the skin that can appear red, blue, or purple. They are generally harmless, though many patients find them distracting. Laser treatment may reduce their appearance on the face and legs, and most patients describe the sessions as quick and comfortable. Results vary, and a consultation confirms whether it suits you.

faqs.question: Are spider veins a health concern?
faqs.answer: They're generally harmless, though many patients find them distracting. Treatment is typically for cosmetic reasons, and your physician will assess your specific case.

faqs.question: Where on the body can spider veins be treated?
faqs.answer: The face and legs are common treatment areas. Your physician will assess whether treatment is appropriate for the area you want treated.

faqs.question: What causes the discolouration in spider veins?
faqs.answer: They're damaged blood vessels under the skin, which can appear red, blue, or purple.

fields.summary: Sun spots, liver spots, and uneven pigmentation build up after years of sun exposure. Laser treatment at Blue Diamond Medical may reduce how visible they are and even out skin tone. The number of sessions depends on the depth and extent of the pigmentation, and results vary between patients.

faqs.question: What causes sun spots and pigmentation?
faqs.answer: Years of sun exposure. Sun spots, liver spots, and uneven pigmentation build up gradually over time.

faqs.question: What treatments address sun damage and pigmentation?
faqs.answer: Laser skin treatments and Ultra may help with sun damage and uneven pigmentation. Your physician will assess the areas you want treated.

faqs.question: Is sun damage/pigmentation the same as "liver spots"?
faqs.answer: Liver spots are one common form of this — both are addressed by the same treatment pathway.

fields.summary: Cynosure's Elite iQ™ laser uses the Skintel™ melanin reader to help practitioners select treatment settings for a range of skin types. Individual suitability is assessed before treatment.
fields.safety_note: The melanin-reading step exists specifically to support safe treatment across a range of skin types; individual suitability is still assessed during a consultation.
fields.how_it_works: Before treatment, the Skintel™ device measures your skin's melanin level. The practitioner uses this reading to help select suitable Elite iQ™ laser settings.
fields.what_it_addresses: Unwanted hair, across a range of skin types and treatment areas, made possible by the melanin-reading calibration step.
fields.appointment_involves: A Skintel™ reading followed by laser passes over the treatment area. All Elite iQ™ treatments are performed at Citizen Studio, not the West Springs clinic — see the laser hair removal treatment page for the address.

faqs.question: What makes Elite iQ™ different from a standard laser hair removal device?
faqs.answer: The Skintel™ melanin reader — it measures your skin's melanin directly rather than relying on a general skin-type estimate, which is what allows the laser settings to be calibrated to you specifically.

faqs.question: Where are Elite iQ™ treatments performed?
faqs.answer: At Citizen Studio, a separate location from the West Springs clinic.

faqs.question: Is Elite iQ™ suitable for every skin type?
faqs.answer: The Skintel™ calibration step is designed to support treatment across a range of skin types, but individual suitability is confirmed during a consultation.

faqs.question: What's the manufacturer of the Elite iQ™ device?
faqs.answer: Cynosure.

faqs.question: How do I book a consultation for a treatment using this device?
faqs.answer: Book a consultation through Mikata — see the laser hair removal treatment page for the direct link.

fields.summary: A radiofrequency microneedling system used for skin tightening and smoothing on the face and body, including fine lines and skin laxity after weight loss or childbirth. Suitability is assessed during a consultation.
fields.how_it_works: Potenza combines microneedling — fine needles creating controlled micro-injuries in the skin — with radiofrequency energy delivered through those same needles, adding a tightening effect to the skin's natural response to micro-injury.
fields.what_it_addresses: Skin tightening and smoothing across the body, including fine lines or laxity following rapid weight loss or after childbirth.

faqs.question: What's the difference between Potenza and standard microneedling?
faqs.answer: Potenza adds radiofrequency energy delivered through the needles, combining the micro-injury response of standard microneedling with an additional tightening effect.

faqs.question: Who is Potenza treatment suited for?
faqs.answer: It's commonly used for skin tightening after rapid weight loss or childbirth, and for fine lines generally — suitability for your specific goals is confirmed during a consultation.

faqs.question: Which treatment uses the Potenza device?
faqs.answer: RF Microneedling.

faqs.question: What's the manufacturer of the Potenza device?
faqs.answer: Cynosure.

fields.summary: A non-invasive radiofrequency device used for skin tightening and firming on the face and body. Downtime is usually minimal; individual responses vary.
fields.how_it_works: TempSure uses radiofrequency energy to gently heat the deeper layers of the skin, encouraging a natural tightening and firming response without breaking the skin's surface.
fields.what_it_addresses: Skin tightening and firming across the body.

faqs.question: Does TempSure treatment involve any downtime?
faqs.answer: There is little to no downtime — the treatment is non-invasive, and most patients return to their usual activities right away.

faqs.question: How does TempSure tighten skin without surgery?
faqs.answer: It heats the deeper layers of the skin using radiofrequency energy, which encourages the skin's own natural tightening response.

faqs.question: Which treatment uses the TempSure device?
faqs.answer: Radiofrequency treatment.

fields.summary: TempSure Vitalia is a radiofrequency device. Women with pelvic floor or sexual health concerns can discuss their symptoms and suitable treatment options with a physician.
fields.how_it_works: TempSure Vitalia delivers temperature-controlled radiofrequency energy to tissue. A physician must assess the proposed use, suitability, risks and expected benefits.
fields.what_it_addresses: Pelvic floor issues and sexual health concerns women may experience at various ages and life stages.

faqs.question: Is TempSure Vitalia surgical?
faqs.answer: No — it is a non-surgical treatment that uses radiofrequency energy.

faqs.question: Who might consider TempSure Vitalia?
faqs.answer: Women experiencing pelvic floor or sexual health concerns at any age or life stage — suitability is assessed during a consultation.

fields.summary: A low-downtime laser that rejuvenates skin, giving it a brighter tone and improved texture, with treatments customized to your needs and schedule.
fields.how_it_works: Ultra is a laser treatment that works on the skin's surface layers to improve tone and texture, with a low-downtime profile.
fields.what_it_addresses: Overall skin tone and texture, with treatments customized to individual needs and scheduling.

faqs.question: How much downtime does an Ultra treatment involve?
faqs.answer: Ultra has a low-downtime profile compared to more intensive resurfacing lasers, and treatments are customized to your schedule.

faqs.question: What does Ultra treatment improve?
faqs.answer: Skin tone and texture, giving a brighter, smoother appearance.

fields.summary: Long-lasting hair reduction on suitable areas of the face and body using the Cynosure Elite+™ laser system. Treatment areas and suitability are assessed during consultation.
fields.preparation: Shave the treatment area beforehand so the laser's energy is delivered effectively.
fields.how_it_works: Hair grows in a three-phase cycle: anagen (active growth), catagen (a brief transition when the hair follicle regresses) and telogen (resting). The laser emits light energy absorbed by melanin in the hair follicle and shaft, damaging the follicle and reducing regrowth. Follicles in the anagen phase respond best, so multiple treatments are needed.
fields.comfort_level: You may feel cold air and a slight snapping sensation and hear a beep during treatment.
fields.result_timeline: Hairs present at the time of treatment fall out over the following weeks. Regrowth becomes thinner and lighter with each subsequent treatment; multiple sessions are needed since not all hairs are actively growing at once.
fields.service_location_note: All Elite iQ™ treatments are performed exclusively at Citizen Studio, 45 Greenbriar Dr NW, Calgary, AB T3B 5N4 — not at the West Springs clinic.

faqs.question: How does Elite iQ™ work?
faqs.answer: Elite iQ™ uses the Skintel™ melanin reader to help the practitioner select settings for your skin. Suitability depends on your skin, hair and treatment area.

faqs.question: Is this treatment right for me?
faqs.answer: Elite iQ™ can treat a range of skin types and body areas. Your physician will assess your skin, hair and medical history to determine whether treatment is appropriate.

faqs.question: How many treatments will I need?
faqs.answer: Treatment times vary by area but typically take less than 30 minutes. Speak to your provider for a consultation to discuss treatment areas.

fields.summary: Laser treatment for a smoother complexion, brighter sun-damaged skin, benign pigmented lesions, and visible face and leg veins. Each protocol is tailored to your skin tone and the concern being treated.
fields.preparation: Avoid sun exposure for one week before a Laser Facial treatment.
fields.how_it_works: A Laser Facial is suited to sun-damaged skin, red or ruddy complexions, light telangiectasia (spider veins), and uneven pigmentation — most often on the face but usable almost anywhere on the body. Each protocol is tailored to skin tone and needs.
fields.suggested_course: Laser Facial: 3–6 treatments usually required for lasting results. Benign pigmented lesions: more even colour is often visible in as few as 2 treatments, with a full course of 4 at 3–4 week intervals. Vascular treatments (spider veins): often clear in as few as 2 treatments, spaced 4–8 weeks apart.

faqs.question: What skin concerns can laser skin treatments address?
faqs.answer: Sun-damaged skin, red or ruddy complexions, light spider veins, uneven pigmentation, and benign pigmented lesions.

faqs.question: Is treatment only for the face?
faqs.answer: It's most often used on the face, but the underlying laser technology can be used almost anywhere on the body.

faqs.question: How should I prepare for a Laser Facial?
faqs.answer: Avoid sun exposure for one week beforehand.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Laser Facial usually take?
faqs.answer: Usually 3–6 treatments for lasting results.

faqs.question: How many sessions for pigmented lesions or spider veins specifically?
faqs.answer: Benign pigmented lesions: more even colour is often visible in as few as 2 treatments, with a full course of 4 at 3–4 week intervals. Vascular treatments (spider veins): often clear in as few as 2 treatments, spaced 4–8 weeks apart.

faqs.question: Is each treatment protocol the same for every patient?
faqs.answer: No — each protocol is tailored to skin tone and individual needs.

fields.summary: Platelet-rich plasma injected into the scalp to stimulate inactive hair follicles and support denser, fuller growth. Performed by Dr. Farhat; results vary between patients.
fields.downtime: Sessions are quick with little to no downtime.
fields.duration: 30 to 60 minutes depending on the treatment area.
fields.who_its_for: Individuals noticing thinning hair or early hair loss.
fields.how_it_works: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is prepared from the patient's own blood. After a blood draw, the blood is processed to concentrate platelets in plasma. The platelets release growth factors involved in tissue repair. PRP is injected into the scalp to support hair growth; results vary.
fields.suggested_course: Most people benefit from a series of 3–4 treatments spaced a few weeks apart; maintenance sessions may be recommended.

faqs.question: Who performs PRP at Blue Diamond Medical?
faqs.answer: PRP treatments are performed by Dr. Farhat.

fields.summary: PRP used topically or via microinjections to smooth fine lines and wrinkles, improve tone and elasticity, and reduce the appearance of acne scars and pigmentation.
fields.duration: 30 to 60 minutes depending on the treatment area.
fields.how_it_works: Platelet-rich plasma prepared from the patient's own blood is applied to the skin or delivered by microinjections. Platelet-derived growth factors may support collagen production and skin renewal; results vary.
fields.suggested_course: Most people benefit from a series of 3–4 treatments spaced a few weeks apart; maintenance sessions may be recommended.

faqs.question: Why is PRP skin rejuvenation sometimes called a "vampire facial"?
faqs.answer: Because it uses the patient's own blood — plasma is separated and applied topically or via microinjections.

faqs.question: What can PRP skin rejuvenation address?
faqs.answer: Fine lines and wrinkles, skin tone and elasticity, acne scars, and pigmentation.

faqs.question: Does this use any synthetic additives?
faqs.answer: PRP is prepared from your own blood. Ask your physician which preparation products are used and whether anything is added as part of your treatment.

faqs.question: How long does a session take, and how many will I need?
faqs.answer: 30 to 60 minutes depending on the treatment area. Most people benefit from a series of 3–4 treatments spaced a few weeks apart, with maintenance sessions sometimes recommended.

fields.summary: Non-invasive tightening and smoothing of skin all over the body using RF waves (TempSure), improving tone and reducing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.
fields.downtime: Downtime is not typically expected, although individual responses vary. Most patients can return to their usual activities right away. Follow your clinician's advice about sunscreen after treatment.
fields.duration: Face and neck treatments (handheld roller over face, neck, and décolletage) take 40–90 minutes depending on area. Body areas are treated with non-invasive pads over about 20 minutes.
fields.how_it_works: A handheld device passes RF waves across the treatment area in a circular motion, gently raising the skin's temperature. The resulting heat penetrates the skin layers and stimulates collagen and elastin production for firmer, more youthful-looking skin.
fields.comfort_level: Most patients find it comfortable, and often describe a warm, massage-like sensation.
fields.result_timeline: Results are gradual rather than immediate — skin looks fresher within a few days, but the most noticeable results appear about 6–8 weeks after the first treatment.
fields.suggested_course: A course of 3–5 treatments spaced 4–6 weeks apart is recommended. Results may last up to two years, although individual responses vary.

faqs.question: Does radiofrequency treatment hurt?
faqs.answer: Most patients find it comfortable and describe a warm, massage-like sensation rather than pain.

faqs.question: How long does a session take?
faqs.answer: Face and neck treatments take 40–90 minutes depending on the area; body areas are treated with non-invasive pads over about 20 minutes.

faqs.question: Is there any downtime?
faqs.answer: Virtually none — you can return to your usual activities right away. A medical-grade sunscreen is recommended afterward to protect results.

faqs.question: When will I see results?
faqs.answer: Results are gradual rather than immediate — skin looks fresher within a few days, but the most noticeable results appear roughly 6–8 weeks after the first treatment.

faqs.question: How many sessions are recommended, and how long do results last?
faqs.answer: A course of 3–5 treatments spaced 4–6 weeks apart is recommended. Results may last up to two years, although individual responses vary.

fields.summary: The Potenza RF microneedling system adds radiofrequency energy to mechanical microneedling for enhanced skin tightening alongside the benefits of micro-injury stimulation.
fields.downtime: Downtime is usually minimal. Redness, minor swelling and pinpoint bleeding can occur and typically settle within three days. Minor bumps or, rarely, micro-crusting can also occur. Contact the clinic if you have concerns about your recovery.
fields.duration: Typically around 30 minutes. A topical anaesthetic is applied and can take up to 45 minutes to become fully effective.
fields.how_it_works: RF energy is delivered through small needles into the dermis, heating the underlying layers to stimulate collagen and elastin production and support skin tightening. Treatments are not limited to the face and may help with skin laxity after weight loss. Results vary.
fields.comfort_level: A topical numbing agent removes most of the discomfort. Most patients say they can feel the needles working but do not find it painful. A member of the clinical team stays with you throughout, and treatment can be stopped at any point.
fields.result_timeline: Some changes may be noticeable soon after treatment, with gradual improvement over several weeks and treatments. More than one session is usually recommended.
fields.suggested_course: Three- and five-session packages are recommended to build and maintain firmer, refreshed-looking skin.

faqs.question: Why RF micro-needling vs. non-RF micro-needling?
faqs.answer: Potenza delivers focused RF technology to heat the skin, triggering the body's natural response to increase collagen and elastin production, resulting in enhanced skin revitalization.

fields.summary: TempSure Vitalia is a non-surgical radiofrequency device. If you have pelvic floor or sexual health concerns, a consultation with Dr. Farhat can help assess your symptoms and discuss appropriate treatment options.
fields.who_its_for: Women experiencing pelvic floor or sexual health concerns who want to discuss whether this simple, in-clinic procedure may be right for them.

faqs.question: Can I discuss pelvic floor or sexual health concerns at a consultation?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can discuss these symptoms with Dr. Farhat. Assessment is needed to identify the cause and consider appropriate treatment options.

faqs.question: Is this a surgical procedure?
faqs.answer: No. TempSure Vitalia is a straightforward, non-surgical procedure carried out in the clinic.

faqs.question: Who is this treatment for?
faqs.answer: Women experiencing pelvic floor or sexual health concerns at any age or life stage, who want to discuss whether it may be right for them.

fields.summary: Ultra is a laser treatment used to improve skin tone and texture and address mild to moderate age spots, freckles, sun spots, benign pigmented lesions, sun damage, melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Suitability is assessed during a consultation.
fields.downtime: Mild redness can occur after treatment and usually lessens over the following day. Most patients can resume their usual activities. Skin may feel dry and sandpaper-like for 5–6 days as it exfoliates; full healing may take 5–7 days.
fields.duration: 10–20 minutes depending on the area treated — sometimes called a "Lunchtime Facial."
fields.comfort_level: Discomfort is variable, described as mild to moderate; a topical numbing cream may be applied to minimize it.
fields.result_timeline: Results may appear after a single treatment or require several visits depending on the condition.

faqs.question: What can Ultra treatment address?
faqs.answer: Mild to moderate age spots, freckles, sun spots, benign pigmented lesions, sun damage, melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. Your physician will assess the skin changes before recommending treatment.

faqs.question: Why is Ultra sometimes called a "Lunchtime Facial"?
faqs.answer: Because a session takes only 10–20 minutes depending on the area treated.

faqs.question: What's recovery like after Ultra treatment?
faqs.answer: Mild redness can occur after treatment and usually lessens over the following day. Most patients can resume their usual activities. Skin may feel dry and sandpaper-like for 5–6 days as it exfoliates; full healing may take 5–7 days.

faqs.question: Will one session be enough?
faqs.answer: Results may appear after a single treatment or require several visits, depending on the condition being treated.

fields.summary: When the clinic is closed, patients can access care through a partner Primary Care Network for medical concerns that need prompt attention but are not emergencies.
fields.urgent_care_note: This referral pathway is for urgent, non-emergency needs only — it is not a substitute for calling 911 in a true emergency.

faqs.question: What counts as an urgent, non-emergency need?
faqs.answer: Concerns that need attention before your next scheduled appointment but aren't life-threatening — for example a worsening infection or a medication question. A true medical emergency always means 911 or the nearest emergency department, not this pathway.

faqs.question: Which Primary Care Network do I contact?
faqs.answer: It depends on your family doctor: Dr. Reem Hamdi's patients are referred to Mosaic Primary Care Network, and patients of all other Blue Diamond family physicians are referred to Calgary West Central Primary Care Network.

faqs.question: Does this apply to every patient at the clinic?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every Blue Diamond patient has an after-hours pathway: Dr. Reem Hamdi's patients are referred to Mosaic Primary Care Network, and patients of all other Blue Diamond family physicians are referred to Calgary West Central Primary Care Network.

faqs.question: Is there a cost for after-hours PCN care?
faqs.answer: Contact the relevant Primary Care Network directly for their current fee and coverage information — this isn't something our clinic bills for, since the care is delivered by the PCN partner.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure whether it's an emergency?
faqs.answer: When in doubt, treat it as an emergency and call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department. It's always safer to be assessed by emergency services than to wait.

fields.summary: Ongoing care for chronic conditions through your family physician. All Blue Diamond family physicians provide chronic disease management.
fields.who_its_for: Patients living with an ongoing health condition that needs regular monitoring and a coordinated care plan.

faqs.question: Is chronic disease management covered by Alberta Health?
faqs.answer: Medically necessary physician care is covered for eligible patients under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP). Coverage for medications and other services is separate.

faqs.question: What kinds of conditions does this cover?
faqs.answer: Any ongoing health condition that needs regular monitoring and a coordinated plan — your family physician will discuss what that looks like for your specific situation.

faqs.question: Do I need to see a particular physician for chronic disease management?
faqs.answer: No — every Blue Diamond family physician provides chronic-disease management as part of general family medicine. Book with whichever of our family physicians you are registered with.

faqs.question: How often will I need to be seen?
faqs.answer: This depends entirely on your specific condition and care plan — your physician will set a monitoring schedule that's appropriate for you.

faqs.question: How do I book a chronic disease management visit?
faqs.answer: If you are already registered with one of our family physicians, book with your doctor through Mikata. New patients and walk-ins can book online through Skip the Waiting Room, call the clinic, or come in — walk-ins are welcome.

fields.summary: Eye disease screening at our Calgary clinic through Euclid Telehealth, with referral based on your doctor's assessment.
fields.who_its_for: Patients referred by their doctor, particularly people with diabetes or a family history of eye disease.
fields.contact_note: Euclid Telehealth patient support: patientsupport@euclidtelehealth.org or 1-800-511-5661.
fields.how_appointments_work: Based on your doctor's recommendation, Euclid Telehealth will contact you directly to schedule your screening.

faqs.question: Is the eye disease screening covered by Alberta Health?
faqs.answer: Eligible eye disease screening is covered by Alberta Health. Euclid Telehealth can confirm your eligibility and any costs before your appointment.

faqs.question: How do I get a screening appointment?
faqs.answer: Your family doctor refers you based on clinical need; Euclid Telehealth then contacts you directly to schedule the visit, which takes place on-site at our clinic once a month.

faqs.question: What does the screening involve?
faqs.answer: It's a non-invasive screening that takes about 20 minutes, aimed at early detection of eye disease before symptoms appear.

faqs.question: Who should consider this screening?
faqs.answer: People with diabetes or a family history of eye disease may benefit from screening. Your doctor can assess whether a referral is appropriate.

faqs.question: What happens if the screening finds something?
faqs.answer: Euclid Telehealth provides guidance on next steps, which may include further testing or a referral, depending on what's found.

faqs.question: Who can I contact with questions about my screening?
faqs.answer: Euclid Telehealth's patient support team handles screening-specific questions directly — see their contact details above.

fields.summary: Minor procedures at the clinic include suture placement and removal, minor skin lesion excision, and joint injections. All of our family physicians provide these procedures. Book by phone or in person.

faqs.question: Are minor procedures covered by Alberta Health?
faqs.answer: Coverage depends on the procedure and whether it is medically necessary. The clinic can confirm Alberta Health coverage and any uninsured fees before your appointment.

faqs.question: What minor procedures are available?
faqs.answer: Suture placement and removal, minor skin lesion excision, and intra-articular injections for degenerative knee, shoulder, and ankle conditions. All of our family physicians provide these.

faqs.question: How do I book a minor procedure?
faqs.answer: Minor procedures cannot be booked online. Call the clinic or come in to reception, and we will schedule the procedure with one of our family physicians.

faqs.question: Is this the same as a walk-in visit?
faqs.answer: No — minor procedures are scheduled appointments rather than walk-in visits. Arrange one by calling the clinic or asking at reception.

fields.summary: Assessment and management of pain through your family physician.

faqs.question: Is pain management covered by Alberta Health?
faqs.answer: Medically necessary physician care is covered for eligible patients under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP). Coverage for medications and other services is separate.

faqs.question: What kind of pain can I discuss with my family doctor?
faqs.answer: Any ongoing or recurring pain — your family physician will assess it and discuss an appropriate management approach as part of your care.

faqs.question: For minor in-clinic procedures related to pain, like joint injections, who provides those?
faqs.answer: Our family physicians perform intra-articular injections for degenerative knee, shoulder, and ankle conditions in-house — see the Minor Procedures page for details. These are booked by phone or in person, not online.

faqs.question: How do I book a pain management appointment?
faqs.answer: If you are registered with one of our family physicians, book with your doctor through Mikata. New patients and walk-ins can book online through Skip the Waiting Room, call the clinic, or come in.

fields.summary: "Prevention is better than cure" is at the core of how we practise — from vaccination to Dr. Saeed's clinical focus on preventive medicine and early intervention.

faqs.question: What's included in preventive care here?
faqs.answer: Vaccination, preventive medicine and early-intervention care, and referral for eye disease screening when appropriate.

faqs.question: Is preventive care covered by Alberta Health?
faqs.answer: Medically necessary physician care is covered for eligible patients under the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP). Some vaccines and other services may have separate costs; ask the clinic before your appointment.

faqs.question: Do I need to see Dr. Saeed specifically for preventive care?
faqs.answer: Preventive medicine and early intervention are particular clinical interests of Dr. Saeed's, but preventive care is available from any of our family physicians.

fields.overview: A lightweight, oil-free moisturizer enriched with vitamins C and E.
fields.how_to_use: Apply to face (and neck if desired) as the moisturizing step of your routine.
fields.what_it_is: A daily lightweight moisturizer.
fields.routine_placement: As the moisturizing step of a routine, for those who prefer a lighter finish.

faqs.question: Is this oil-free?
faqs.answer: Yes, per manufacturer information.

faqs.question: How is this different from Rejuvenative Moisturizer?
faqs.answer: Both are moisturizers in this catalogue; this one is positioned as a lighter, sheer finish — ask the clinic which suits your skin type.

faqs.question: What vitamins does it contain?
faqs.answer: Vitamins C and E, per manufacturer information.

faqs.question: When do I apply it?
faqs.answer: As the moisturizing step of your routine.

fields.overview: A morning antioxidant serum combining vitamin C and vitamin E, formulated to release gradually through the day.
fields.how_to_use: Apply a single pump into the hand and gently apply to the entire face (neck and chest if desired) each morning.
fields.what_it_is: A vitamin C and E antioxidant serum for daytime use.
fields.routine_placement: Each morning after cleansing, toning, and (if used) TNS Recovery Complex, and before moisturizer.

faqs.question: When should I apply this?
faqs.answer: In the morning, after cleansing/toning and before moisturizer.

faqs.question: What vitamins does it contain?
faqs.answer: Vitamin C (as Ascorbic Acid and Tetrahexyldecyl Ascorbate) and vitamin E (as Tocopherol), per manufacturer information.

faqs.question: Should I still wear sunscreen with this?
faqs.answer: An antioxidant serum doesn't replace sunscreen — daily sun protection is a separate, important step.

faqs.question: How much do I use?
faqs.answer: A single pump, applied to the entire face and optionally neck and chest.
